test.title: Reading the rings of a shell

paragraphs.text: A clam shell grows a thin band every year, much like a tree. Because some clams live for centuries, a single shell can record the temperature of the sea from before the first thermometers were made.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Working with shells is slow. Each band is thinner than a hair, and the shell must be cut, polished and photographed under a microscope before the bands can be counted and measured.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The results have been useful. Shell records from the north Atlantic match ship logs for the last two hundred years, which gives scientists confidence in the older parts of the record, where no logs exist.
paragraphs.label: C
